identity: A drawing board shows a figure, scale, chart, map, route, or field of markers where the user clicks one precise point.

scenarios.name: center
scenarios.screen: The board shows one circle, ring, filled disc, or circular arc. No clicked point is marked, and no picker or popup is open.
never: A center marker already placed on the board.
Several separate figures to choose between.
A shape picker open over the board.

arrangements.text: One complete circle sits near the middle of the board.
A circular arc sits in the left portion of the board, with its implied center inside that portion.
One ring sits in the upper portion of the board, leaving open board space below it.

scenarios.hint: Show the requested circle or circular arc only; do not mark or reveal its true center. Empty canvas surrounds it.

scenarios.name: midpoint
scenarios.screen: The board shows two marked endpoints, sometimes labeled A and B, with space between them for the midpoint click. No clicked point is marked.
never: A midpoint marker already placed between the endpoints.
Three or more endpoints in the same problem.
A draggable handle on the segment.

arrangements.text: The two endpoints lie diagonally across the middle of the board.
A sits to the left of B on one horizontal line.
Both endpoints sit in the lower portion of the board, with open board space above.

scenarios.hint: Show two distinct labeled endpoints A and B without marking their midpoint. Preserve straight Euclidean geometry.

scenarios.name: bisect
scenarios.screen: Two rays meet at one vertex, and a dotted circle surrounds the vertex. The board has no clicked point or movable angle tool.
never: A point already placed on the angle bisector.
A filled wedge showing the answer.
Multiple unrelated angles on the board.

arrangements.text: The vertex sits near the middle, with two rays extending away from it and a dotted circle around it.
The vertex, rays, and dotted circle occupy the left portion of the board.
The vertex, rays, and dotted circle occupy the upper portion of the board.

scenarios.hint: Show two rays meeting at V, labeled A and B, and a small dotted exclusion circle centered at V; do not reveal the bisector answer.

scenarios.name: right-angle
scenarios.screen: The board shows points A and B joined by a segment, with a dotted circle around B. No third point has been placed.
never: Point C already placed on the board.
A completed right-angle marker at B.
Several candidate points offered as buttons.

arrangements.text: A and B sit across the middle of the board, with the dotted circle centered on B.
A sits left of B on a horizontal segment, and the dotted circle surrounds B.
A, B, and the dotted circle occupy the right portion of the board.

scenarios.hint: Show segment AB with filled dot at B and a small dotted exclusion circle about B; leave space for a point C perpendicular to AB outside the circle. No solution marker.

scenarios.name: axis
scenarios.screen: The board shows one labeled ruler or one chart with axes and plotted data. The target position has no clicked marker, and no menu or popup is open.
never: A marker already placed at the requested value.
An editable numeric answer field.
A ruler and a chart shown together as separate tasks.

arrangements.text: A horizontal ruler runs across the board with scale labels beside its ticks.
A vertical ruler runs through the board with scale labels beside its ticks.
A line chart fills a plot rectangle, with values along the bottom axis and a series running through it.
A coordinate chart fills a plot rectangle, with labeled horizontal and vertical axes.

scenarios.name: map
scenarios.screen: The board shows either a labeled latitude and longitude grid or a map of named streets. No location pin has been placed, and no map picker is open.
never: A pin already placed at the target location.
A search box for entering an address.
Several separate maps to choose between.

arrangements.text: Latitude lines cross longitude lines across the board, with their labels at the grid edges.
Named streets cross within the board, with their names placed along the streets.
A wide latitude and longitude grid spans the board, with more horizontal room between its left and right edges.

scenarios.name: path-mid
scenarios.screen: A grid-aligned route connects A and B through several turns. There is no clicked marker on the route.
never: A halfway marker already placed on the route.
A freehand curve replacing the grid-aligned route.
A second route offered as an alternative.

arrangements.text: The route winds across the middle of the board from A to B.
The entire route occupies the left portion of the board.
The entire route occupies the lower portion of the board.

scenarios.name: dense
scenarios.screen: The board contains roughly 40 small markers, identified by labels or by one marker with a different shape or color. No marker has been selected by a click.
never: A selection marker already placed on a dot.
Hundreds of markers on the board.
A list of answer buttons replacing the dot field.

arrangements.text: Small labeled dots are spread across the board.
The marker field occupies the right portion of the board.
The marker field occupies the upper portion of the board, with one square among the dots.
